hero.headline: Port St. Lucie's Southern Grove named one of America's fastest-growing neighborhoods
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code has earned recognition from RentCafe as one of the fastest-growing in the nation, with Southern Grove leading the charge. The neighborhood, which was virtually nonexistent a decade ago, has transformed into a thriving community. Housing inventory in the area has increased by 177 percent, representing one of the largest growth spurts in Florida. The neighborhood has also attracted residents who are highly educated and maintain strong homeownership rates.

The explosive growth of Southern Grove stems partly from its deliberate design as one of four planned neighborhoods created to draw people to the area and encourage them to remain. The strategy appears to be working, as major employers have made Southern Grove a hub for job opportunities. FedEx and Amazon have both established operations there, with Amazon demonstrating its confidence in the area by planning to close its current facility later this year and construct a larger replacement.

According to Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, Florida's emergence as a hotbed for new neighborhoods reflects several competitive advantages. The state ranks second only to Texas for up-and-coming communities, largely due to its favorable tax environment and housing costs that remain lower than major markets like New York and California. Beyond these factors, sustained investment in infrastructure has spurred construction activity throughout the state's growing suburbs.

Other Florida communities have also caught the attention of RentCafe. Ponte Vedra Beach claimed the top position on the organization's "America's 50 Newest Neighborhoods" list, appealing to families, retirees, and young professionals alike. Both Daytona Beach and the St. Augustine area made the top 50, receiving praise for their excellent schools and robust housing demand. This recognition underscores Florida's broader appeal as a destination for growth and development, with Southern Grove standing out as a particularly striking example of how strategic planning and economic investment can transform a region.

cards.headline: Florida House asks Supreme Court to strike down Fair Districts Amendment, allow new congressional map
cards.teaser: Attorneys for the Florida House are asking the state Supreme Court to declare the Fair Districts Amendment unconstitutional and allow a new congressional map to.
cards.body:
Attorneys for the Florida House are asking the state Supreme Court to declare the Fair Districts Amendment unconstitutional, arguing it is impossible to comply with the amendment and draw a legal map. In a brief filed by attorney Andy Bardos, counsel for the Florida House, attorneys contend the 16-year-old amendment approved by voters in 2010 no longer aligns with a federal ruling that raised the threshold for considering race in redistricting. The brief argues the Fair Districts Amendment's racial classifications treat people differently based on race and compel the Legislature to design districts where members of certain races will control elections. House attorneys assert the amendment's racial elements cannot be separated from its prohibition on partisan gerrymandering, meaning the entire amendment should be invalidated.

Voting rights groups led by the Equal Ground Education Fund are challenging a congressional map designed by Gov. Ron DeSantis' office, arguing it violates the amendment's ban on partisan gerrymandering. Plaintiffs note mapmakers admitted using partisan data and released the map first to Fox News with districts colored to show 2024 presidential election performance. A Leon County Circuit Judge appointed by DeSantis ruled against an injunction to block the map. In response, attorney Marc Elias' firm filed a brief on behalf of plaintiffs, arguing the House position is not sensible and that no court has found racial defects in the 2022 map previously designed by DeSantis' office.

cards.headline: Florida property tax referendum faces up to five constitutional challenges before November vote
cards.teaser: A statewide referendum to lower property taxes by raising the homestead exemption could face multiple legal challenges on issues including ballot language, home rule, and unfunded mandates.
cards.body:
The referendum on lowering property taxes in Florida may face a state constitutional challenge on several fronts, according to former Florida state Sen. Jeff Brandes. In a Saturday social media post, Brandes listed five possible legal challenges to the referendum that would raise the homestead exemption for homeowners to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Those possible challenges include ballot language, equal protection, uniformity, home rule, and unfunded mandates. "I think there's questions about home rule. Think there's questions about unfunded mandates. I think there's questions about taxing uniformity. There's a variety of questions," Brandes told WPTV on Monday.

State Rep. Toby Overdorf, R-Stuart, emphasized the constitutional significance of the measure after the vote was approved in special session last week. "We need to first of all remember this is not a normal bill. This is a joint resolution that changes the Constitution," Overdorf told WPTV. He said he does expect a legal challenge, but multiple challenges could put the courts under pressure with a vote scheduled for Election Day in November. Brandes said the courts will have to consolidate these matters and address a handful of really interesting questions. At this point, there are no lawsuits filed against the referendum, but many expect that to happen once the actual question for voters is completed.

cards.headline: 2-year-old drowns in Fort Pierce backyard pool after leaving home unnoticed
cards.teaser: A 2-year-old drowned over the weekend in Fort Pierce after the child was found unresponsive in a swimming pool, police said.
cards.body:
A 2-year-old drowned in Fort Pierce over the weekend after being found unresponsive in a swimming pool. The drowning occurred at a home in the 2600 block of Citrus Avenue on Saturday. According to a preliminary police investigation, the child was able to unlock a door and leave the residence unnoticed while family members were inside. When family members realized the child was missing, they searched the property and discovered the child unresponsive in the swimming pool. Family members immediately began administering first aid until Fort Pierce police officers arrived at the scene. Officers worked to save the child, who was then transported to a local hospital for emergency medical treatment. The child later succumbed to injuries sustained in the incident.

This drowning is the latest in a series of similar incidents in the area. A 2-year-old drowned in a Greenacres canal in March, and another 2-year-old drowned in Palm Beach Gardens in May. The Fort Pierce incident remains under investigation.

cards.headline: 6.1 magnitude earthquake off Cuba shakes Florida from Miami to Jacksonville, triggers evacuations
cards.teaser: A 6.1 magnitude earthquake centered off the west-northwest coast of Cuba on Tuesday prompted building evacuations across Miami and was felt as far north as Jacksonville.
cards.body:
A 6.1 magnitude earthquake centered off the west-northwest coast of Cuba sent tremors across Florida on Tuesday, triggering evacuations in Miami and being felt as far north as Jacksonville. The quake interrupted daily activities at multiple buildings throughout the region, prompting immediate safety responses from local authorities.

Students and staff at Fusion Academy in Miami were among the first to evacuate when the earthquake struck. The evacuation alarm differed noticeably from routine fire drills, with an urgent message declaring this was not a standard drill. Maria Torrado, a student at the academy, noted that people on the upper floors experienced the shaking more intensely than those on lower levels. The heightened urgency of the alarm startled many students who were accustomed to regular fire safety exercises.

Reactions to the earthquake varied across different locations. Students at the Swatch Watchmaking School were evacuated but did not initially understand what was happening. Jack Hodapp reported that people in the break room felt the quaking sensation, but those in other areas had no idea why they were being asked to leave the building. Some students initially thought their coworkers were pranking them. Juan Cardona, who was also evacuated, initially suspected criminal activity was unfolding before learning from conversations with others that an earthquake centered near Cuba had caused the commotion.

The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office responded by establishing a command center and blocking off streets near affected buildings as a precautionary measure. After buildings were inspected for safety, evacuated individuals were allowed to return inside. The National Weather Service assessed the situation and confirmed there was no tsunami risk resulting from the earthquake. No injuries were reported in Florida from the seismic event. The swift response from local authorities and the rapid return to normal operations meant that despite the disruption and initial confusion, the situation was resolved without significant consequences for the affected communities.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County enforces new 45-day anchoring limit to clear abandoned vessels from waterways
hero.body:
St. Lucie County rolled out new anchoring restrictions on June 1 designed to address the growing problem of abandoned vessels in local waterways. The regulations apply to two anchor limitation areas: the Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor near the South Causeway Bridge. Under these rules, boaters cannot anchor a vessel for more than 45 consecutive days within any six-month period without leaving all designated anchoring limitation areas for at least 24 hours.

County officials have noticed an uptick in derelict vessels cluttering these important waterways. Last year alone, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission collected approximately two dozen abandoned vessels from the area. According to Erick Gill with St. Lucie County, the new restrictions serve a practical purpose by improving navigation. "We need to make sure that highway for vessels is clear and free for other vessels to come and go," Gill explained. By limiting how long boats can remain anchored in one spot, the county aims to prevent vessels from becoming permanent fixtures that obstruct traffic and access.

Beyond navigation concerns, abandoned vessels pose serious environmental threats to the lagoon ecosystem. James Beams with St. Lucie County Port, Inlet and Beaches highlighted these dangers in an earlier interview, noting that long-abandoned vessels create multiple pollution risks. "There's a lot of environmental concern with the diesel and oil tanks and then holding tanks," Beams said. When these vessels deteriorate or leak, they release harmful contaminants into the water. Gill emphasized that the new anchoring limits will help prevent these pollutants from contaminating the waterway.

The Indian River Lagoon is an ecologically vital area supporting over 4,000 species of animals, plants, and birds. Protecting this biodiversity is central to the county's motivation for implementing the restrictions. "We want to make sure we're protecting it," Gill said. Boaters who need detailed information about the anchor limitation areas can access a site map through St. Lucie County. The new rules represent the county's effort to balance recreational boating access with environmental preservation and waterway management.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Commissioner Sara Baxter announces congressional run for newly drawn District 22
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County Mayor Sara Baxter will drop out of her county commission race to run for Congress, creating an open race for the District 6 seat representing western Palm Beach County.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County Mayor and District 6 Commissioner Sara Baxter announced on Monday that she will be running for Congress. She confirmed to WPTV's western Palm Beach County reporter, Michael Hoffman, that she will drop out of the commission race to pursue a congressional seat. Baxter will aim for Florida's newly drawn District 22 seat, saying the new district "blesses me with the opportunity to work with President Trump to stop illegal migrant crime, protect our elections, cut taxes, slash red tape and bloated bureaucracy, protect hard working farmers, our food supply chain, support our great military and veterans, and defend our Second Amendment rights."

Baxter was elected to the District 6 seat in 2022 representing parts of western Palm Beach County including Royal Palm Beach, Loxahatchee Groves, Acreage, Wellington, Westlake, Belle Glade, South Bay, Pahokee, and West Lake Worth. Before her election, Baxter held no political office and ran a small business with her husband, Brian. President Donald Trump has endorsed Baxter, calling her "A true MAGA Warrior" and highlighting her work to grow the economy, cut taxes and regulations, stop migrant crime, and defend the Second Amendment. Her announcement creates an open race for the District 6 county commission seat. The newly drawn Congressional District 22 is expected to be one of South Florida's closely watched races in the 2026 election cycle.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County implements 45-day anchoring limits in Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor
hero.teaser: New restrictions took effect June 1 limiting vessels to 45 consecutive days of anchoring in designated areas near the South Causeway Bridge.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County has introduced new restrictions on vessel anchoring to address concerns about abandoned boats in local waterways. Starting June 1, the county established two anchor limitation areas in the Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor near the South Causeway Bridge. Under these new rules, boaters cannot anchor a vessel for more than 45 consecutive days within any six-month period in these designated areas. Anyone who wants to anchor longer must leave all anchoring limitation areas for at least 24 hours before returning.

The county has been observing an increase in abandoned vessels in these waterways, which prompted the new policy. According to Erick Gill with St. Lucie County, the Florida Wildlife Commission collected around two dozen derelict vessels last year. The anchoring restrictions aim to keep these waterways more navigable for active boating traffic. "We need to make sure that highway for vessels is clear and free for other vessels to come and go," Gill said. By limiting how long vessels can remain stationary, officials hope to prevent derelict boats from cluttering the channels that other boaters need to use.

Environmental protection is another major concern driving the new regulations. When abandoned vessels remain in the water for extended periods, they pose risks to water quality through leaking diesel, oil, and holding tanks. James Beams with St. Lucie County Port, Inlet and Beaches emphasized this threat, noting the environmental consequences of prolonged vessel abandonment. Gill stressed the importance of preventing these pollutants from contaminating the lagoon, which serves as home to an estimated 4,000 species of animals, plants, and birds. "We want to make sure we're protecting it," Gill said.

The anchoring limitation areas represent the county's effort to balance boating access with environmental stewardship and waterway maintenance. By preventing long-term anchoring without breaks, officials believe they can reduce the number of abandoned vessels while protecting the lagoon's ecosystem and ensuring clear navigation for legitimate boating activities. For detailed information about the specific locations of the anchor limitation areas, the county has provided a site map of the designated zones.

cards.headline: Brightline and Tri-Rail offer cheaper alternatives to driving for World Cup matches in Miami
cards.teaser: Fans heading to World Cup matches at Hard Rock Stadium can save money by taking Brightline or Tri-Rail instead of driving and parking.
cards.body:
Hard Rock Stadium will host seven FIFA World Cup 2026 matches in Miami, starting Monday, June 15, when Saudi Arabia takes on Uruguay at 6 p.m. The final Miami match, the third-place match, is scheduled for Saturday, July 18 at 5 p.m. Brightline is the official transit partner for the tournament, offering round-trip tickets ranging from $76 to $150. From the Brightline Aventura Station, the designated transit hub closest to the stadium, Miami-Dade County will provide free Game Day Express shuttle buses directly to the stadium gates. Shuttles operate on a first-come, first-served basis, and riders must show a valid World Cup match ticket for that specific day to board.

Tri-Rail offers a more affordable alternative, with one-way tickets ranging from $2.50 to $6.90 depending on the starting station, and weekend round-trip travel available for $5. Both transit options are significantly cheaper than driving, as parking passes for Hard Rock Stadium must be purchased in advance, with some costing as much as $200. Additional transportation options include taking Metrorail or Tri-Rail to the Miami-Dade Golden Glades Interchange and connecting via Metrobus Route 297. Rideshare services like Uber and Lyft can also drop passengers at designated rideshare zones at the stadium, though surge pricing and longer wait times are expected after matches.

cards.headline: Delray Beach Golf Club renovation reaches 50 percent completion ahead of 2026 reopening
cards.teaser: The $30 million renovation of Delray Beach Golf Club is 50 percent complete as of early June and on track for a November 2026 reopening.
cards.body:
Delray Beach Golf Club's $30 million renovation is halfway complete and on track for a November 2026 reopening. The course has been closed since November 2025 for the project, which aims to restore its historic character while modernizing the facility. City officials confirmed in early June that work is 50 percent finished. The renovation is progressing in phases, with the north 9 holes, known as the Wilson 9, already fully grassed and growing in. The south 9 holes, called the Ross 9, are currently being grassed.

Ronnie Dunayer, a golf instructor who has taught at the course for 20 years, expressed enthusiasm about the progress after visiting the site. "I've been an advocate for improvement for a long time, and in all honesty, it's looking better than anticipated," Dunayer said. She has been teaching at an indoor facility during the closure but looks forward to returning to what will be "a virtually new golf course, but yet have the old integrity." The original course was designed by legendary architects Donald Ross and Dick Wilson. However, Delray Beach resident Maureen Allyn contacted WPTV with concerns that large planting holes being dug for trees near her home could block her golf course view and negatively impact her property value. The city says the $30 million budget remains unchanged.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach resident to cheer for Cape Verde at World Cup in Miami
cards.teaser: Eridjon Dacruz of West Palm Beach will attend Cape Verde's World Cup match against Uruguay in Miami this month as the tiny island nation makes its first World Cup appearance.
cards.body:
Eridjon Dacruz grew up in Cape Verde, an archipelago of 10 islands off the African coast, before moving to West Palm Beach. Cape Verde, which was part of Portugal until gaining independence in the 1970s, has a population of only half a million people. Cape Verdeans are ecstatic over their team, known as the Tubarão Azul or Blue Sharks, making the World Cup field for the first time ever. Dacruz, who has many family members still living in Cape Verde, says it has been the talk of the island.

Dacruz will be at Cape Verde's game against Uruguay in Miami in person, a gift from his girlfriend on their anniversary. She gave him a little box with a handwritten note saying he was going to the World Cup during their anniversary dinner. Cape Verde opens the tournament against Spain, one of the tournament favorites, but Dacruz is confident his team can advance. Making the World Cup will provide the nation's soccer federation with more than $10 million to help develop the next generation of players.

hero.headline: West Palm Beach man heads to Miami to cheer on Cape Verde at World Cup
hero.body:
Eridjon Dacruz of West Palm Beach is traveling to Miami this month to watch Cape Verde compete in the World Cup for the first time in the island nation's history. Dacruz grew up in Cape Verde, an archipelago of 10 islands located off the African coast, before moving to the United States. The island nation has a population of only half a million people and gained independence from Portugal in the 1970s. As one of the smallest countries ever to qualify for the World Cup, Cape Verde's achievement has generated tremendous excitement among its citizens, including Dacruz's family members who still live there.

Cape Verdeans are celebrating their national team, known as the Tubarão Azul or Blue Sharks, reaching the World Cup field. Dacruz expresses amazement at the accomplishment, saying he did not expect it to happen in his lifetime given the country's small size. He recalls searching for Cape Verde players in FIFA video games years ago and finding only about two available. The qualification has been the dominant topic of conversation among people on the islands, reflecting how significant this moment is for the nation. Dacruz will attend Cape Verde's match against Uruguay in Miami, a gift from his girlfriend presented during their anniversary dinner in a small box with a handwritten note that read "I'm going to the World Cup."

Cape Verde opens the tournament against Spain, one of the tournament favorites, before facing Uruguay. Dacruz remains optimistic about his team's chances, saying that if they win a couple of games, they can advance far in the competition. He is currently waiting for the newest Cape Verde national jersey to arrive so he can wear it to the game this month. Making the World Cup will provide the nation's soccer federation with more than 10 million dollars to help develop the next generation of players and strengthen the country's soccer program.

During hurricane season, Cape Verde receives significant attention in weather coverage as tropical systems frequently form near the islands before tracking west across the Atlantic toward the United States. According to meteorologist Sami Squires, tropical waves form along the African coast in the region and eventually track across the Atlantic, sometimes heading toward the U.S. These weather patterns make Cape Verde a familiar reference point for people monitoring hurricane season activity.

cards.headline: Four men rescue 324-pound injured sea turtle in Jupiter Sound
cards.teaser: Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony were boating in Jupiter Sound when they spotted an adult female green sea turtle struggling in the Intracoastal Waterway with severe injuries from a boat strike.
cards.body:
Four friends boating in Jupiter Sound became unlikely heroes when they spotted a 324-pound adult female sea turtle struggling in the Intracoastal Waterway. Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony quickly realized the injured turtle was too heavy and badly injured for one person to handle alone. Working together, they tied a rope around the turtle's shell and guided her toward Blowing Rocks Marina in what Savery described as exhausting work requiring "a big effort from each of us." Once out of the water, the extent of the turtle's injuries became clear. Her shell was covered in deep cuts, and her head drooped weakly, revealing signs of a boat strike. The four men named the turtle Zoey.

The Loggerhead Marinelife Center responded to the marina and confirmed Zoey had suffered severe injuries from a vessel strike. Despite the rescue efforts and medical care, Zoey passed away just hours later. Anthony said the turtle "had probably been fighting for hours out there." According to NOAA, sea turtles are at risk of being struck by vessels as they surface to breathe or rest near the surface or in shallow water. The agency estimates hundreds to thousands of sea turtles are struck by vessels in the U.S. annually. In Florida alone, injuries consistent with vessel strikes are observed in 20 to 30 percent of stranded sea turtles, with adult sea turtles particularly vulnerable during nesting season from March through October.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie's Southern Grove named one of America's fastest-growing neighborhoods
cards.teaser: RentCafe named Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code one of the fastest-growing in the country, driven by the Southern Grove neighborhood which has seen housing inventory explode by 177 percent.
cards.body:
Southern Grove, a neighborhood that barely existed ten years ago, has become a major jobs hub in Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code, attracting big-name employers like FedEx and Amazon. Amazon is so committed to the area that they're closing their current facility later this year to build an even bigger one. The neighborhood has seen housing inventory explode by 177%, one of the largest growth spurts in all of Florida. Southern Grove earned high marks for its educated residents and strong homeownership rates, helping RentCafe recognize it as one of the fastest-growing zip codes in the entire country.

Southern Grove was deliberately designed as one of four neighborhoods meant to give people compelling reasons to move there and stay. According to Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, Florida's high number of up-and-coming communities, second only to Texas, reflects the state's favorable tax environment and relatively lower housing costs compared to major markets like New York and California. Sustained infrastructure investment has fueled construction activity in many of these growing suburbs. Other Florida communities are also gaining recognition, with Ponte Vedra Beach claiming the number one spot on RentCafe's "America's 50 Newest Neighborhoods" list. Daytona Beach and the St. Augustine area also cracked the top 50, earning recognition for their excellent schools and strong housing demand.

hero.headline: 'Beetlejuice' the musical runs through Saturday at Kravis Center in West Palm Beach
hero.teaser: The Broadway hit brings its spooky humor and over-the-top visuals to the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall through June 7, with actor Ryan Stajmiger stepping into the iconic striped suit.
hero.body:
Running June 2 through June 7, 'Beetlejuice' the musical has landed at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach. Actor Ryan Stajmiger plays the mischievous demon beloved from Tim Burton's 1988 film. The musical follows Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teen whose life changes after meeting two recently deceased neighbors and a demon with a flair for trouble.

Stajmiger says one of his favorite parts is laughing with the audience. He gets to break the fourth wall and communicate directly to the audience. Very early in the run, he experienced an unexpected moment when his wig change went wrong. He was wearing two wigs and the second wig came off with the first wig, leaving him bald for an entire scene.

Performances include 7:30 p.m. shows on June 3 and June 4, 8 p.m. on June 5, matinee and evening performances on June 6, and a closing matinee on June 7. Tickets start at $34.50, and the safest and most secure way to get them is to buy directly at kravis.org. The show is recommended for ages 13 and up, with parental discretion advised.

cards.headline: Armory Art Center offers summer camps and programs in West Palm Beach
cards.teaser: The Armory Art Center is debuting a lineup of camps and programs designed for artists of all ages, from splatter painting to workshops exploring global styles and cultures.
cards.body:
The Armory Art Center is launching summer camps and programs for artists of all ages this season, according to Education Director Vita Litvak. The creative offerings range from splatter painting inspired by mid-20th-century art movements to workshops exploring global styles and cultures, designed to engage participants from young children to adults.

Summer camp sessions run in various formats through August, with registration available at armoryart.org. The center offers scholarships, Litvak confirmed, ensuring that cost is not a barrier for budding artists. The Armory's broad range of offerings includes youth camps and adult intensives.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Gardens sixth graders teach peers to build computers at free summer camp
cards.teaser: The Weiss School hosts the Kids Teaching Kids Academy, founded by 12-year-old Heath Neer, with 20 participants and five student instructors from Palm Beach Gardens, West Palm Beach and Riviera Beach.
cards.body:
At The Weiss School this week, sixth graders are teaching their peers how to build computers and learn artificial intelligence basics through Kids Teaching Kids Academy, a free program created by 12-year-old founder Heath Neer. The initiative launched last year with five students and has quadrupled in size this summer, with 20 participants and five student instructors from Palm Beach Gardens, West Palm Beach and Riviera Beach. The camp runs June 1-4 and is entirely peer-led, supported by The Weiss School and parent volunteers.

The curriculum includes hands-on assembly of computers that attendees take home free, plus lessons on fundamental AI concepts. The program uses donated parts and community support to keep costs down, with instructors wearing camp shirts and hats to create team spirit. By empowering children to teach one another, organizers aim to close technology access gaps for students who might not otherwise have access to computers. Instructors plan to complete computer builds by week's end and move into demonstrations of AI applications. Organizers hope the program's success will encourage similar peer-led models across Palm Beach County.

cards.headline: Lake Worth Beach to host 80-mile ocean paddle for Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis
cards.body:
More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of the Atlantic Ocean this June as part of the annual Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis. According to event founder Travis Suit, participants will launch from Bimini, Bahamas, at midnight on June 13 and arrive at Lake Worth Beach after 12 to 16 hours of paddling. The event benefits the Piper's Angels Foundation, which Suit established to honor his daughter Piper, who was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at age 4. Suit created the foundation after learning about the respiratory benefits of ocean salt air and has grown it to provide direct support and resources to cystic fibrosis patients and families.

The four-day event begins June 10 with arrivals and a poolside social at Bimini Cove. Thursday includes a 4Ocean beach cleanup and community buffet dinner, while Friday features a Paddle Out Rose Ceremony honoring cystic fibrosis warriors, followed by rest and safety checks before the midnight launch. All paddlers must wear a U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation device, waterproof whistle, and reflective gear during dark hours, with GPS trackers that remain active throughout. Paddlers must raise a minimum of $2,000, while crew and virtual participants have a $500 minimum, with all contributions due by July 31. Spectators are invited to Lake Worth Beach on June 13 for a daylong beach celebration welcoming arriving paddlers. For more information, visit crossingforcysticfibrosis.com and pipersangels.org.

hero.headline: 6.1 magnitude earthquake off Cuba shakes Florida from Miami to Jacksonville, triggers evacuations
hero.teaser: A 6.1 magnitude earthquake centered off the west-northwest coast of Cuba on Tuesday prompted building evacuations across Miami and was felt as far north as Jacksonville.
hero.body:
A 6.1 magnitude earthquake centered off the west-northwest coast of Cuba sent tremors across Florida on Tuesday, triggering evacuations in Miami and being felt as far north as Jacksonville. The quake interrupted daily activities at multiple buildings throughout the region, prompting immediate safety responses from local authorities.

Students and staff at Fusion Academy in Miami were among the first to evacuate when the earthquake struck. The evacuation alarm differed noticeably from routine fire drills, with an urgent message declaring this was not a standard drill. Maria Torrado, a student at the academy, noted that people on the upper floors experienced the shaking more intensely than those on lower levels. The heightened urgency of the alarm startled many students who were accustomed to regular fire safety exercises.

Reactions to the earthquake varied across different locations. Students at the Swatch Watchmaking School were evacuated but did not initially understand what was happening. Jack Hodapp reported that people in the break room felt the quaking sensation, but those in other areas had no idea why they were being asked to leave the building. Some students initially thought their coworkers were pranking them. Juan Cardona, who was also evacuated, initially suspected criminal activity was unfolding before learning from conversations with others that an earthquake centered near Cuba had caused the commotion.

The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office responded by establishing a command center and blocking off streets near affected buildings as a precautionary measure. After buildings were inspected for safety, evacuated individuals were allowed to return inside. The National Weather Service assessed the situation and confirmed there was no tsunami risk resulting from the earthquake. No injuries were reported in Florida from the seismic event. The swift response from local authorities and the rapid return to normal operations meant that despite the disruption and initial confusion, the situation was resolved without significant consequences for the affected communities.

cards.headline: Florida House asks Supreme Court to strike down Fair Districts Amendment, allow new congressional map
cards.teaser: Attorneys for the Florida House are asking the state Supreme Court to declare the Fair Districts Amendment unconstitutional and allow a new congressional map to.
cards.body:
Attorneys for the Florida House are asking the state Supreme Court to declare the Fair Districts Amendment unconstitutional, arguing it is impossible to comply with the amendment and draw a legal map. In a brief filed by attorney Andy Bardos, counsel for the Florida House, attorneys contend the 16-year-old amendment approved by voters in 2010 no longer aligns with a federal ruling that raised the threshold for considering race in redistricting. The brief argues the Fair Districts Amendment's racial classifications treat people differently based on race and compel the Legislature to design districts where members of certain races will control elections. House attorneys assert the amendment's racial elements cannot be separated from its prohibition on partisan gerrymandering, meaning the entire amendment should be invalidated.

Voting rights groups led by the Equal Ground Education Fund are challenging a congressional map designed by Gov. Ron DeSantis' office, arguing it violates the amendment's ban on partisan gerrymandering. Plaintiffs note mapmakers admitted using partisan data and released the map first to Fox News with districts colored to show 2024 presidential election performance. A Leon County Circuit Judge appointed by DeSantis ruled against an injunction to block the map. In response, attorney Marc Elias' firm filed a brief on behalf of plaintiffs, arguing the House position is not sensible and that no court has found racial defects in the 2022 map previously designed by DeSantis' office.

cards.headline: Florida property tax referendum faces up to five constitutional challenges ahead of November vote
cards.teaser: The referendum to lower Florida property taxes may face multiple constitutional challenges before voters decide on the measure in November, according to a former state senator.
cards.body:
Former Florida state Sen. Jeff Brandes told WPTV on Monday that the property tax referendum could face constitutional challenges on multiple fronts, including questions about home rule, unfunded mandates and taxing uniformity. In a Saturday social media post, Brandes outlined five possible legal challenges to the referendum that would raise the homestead exemption for homeowners to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. The challenges include ballot language, equal protection, uniformity, home rule and unfunded mandates.

State Rep. Toby Overdorf, a Stuart Republican, said he expects a legal challenge because this is not a normal bill but a joint resolution that changes the Constitution. The referendum was approved in special session last week and is scheduled for a vote on Election Day in November. Brandes said multiple challenges could put courts under pressure with the November deadline, noting that courts will need to consolidate the cases. No lawsuits have been filed against the referendum yet, but many expect challenges once the actual ballot question for voters is completed.

cards.headline: Hector Mujica nearing exit from Congressional District 28 race after party registration issue
cards.teaser: Hector Mujica is close to withdrawing from the Congressional District 28 race and wants former federal prosecutor Robin Peguero to switch races and replace him, multiple sources confirmed.
cards.body:
Hector Mujica is on the precipice of withdrawing from the Congressional District 28 race after voter registration records revealed he switched his party affiliation from Democrat to no party affiliation on June 4, 2025, before switching back to Democrat on July 26, 2025. Florida statute requires candidates to be registered members of their party for 365 consecutive days to run for that party's nomination. Democratic lawmakers updated the statute with unanimous support in the Legislature this year and Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the measure in early April. Mujica, a former Google executive who raised more than $717,000 on an aborted Senate race, has denied changing his party affiliation or knowing about the change until late last month when the campaign of his primary opponent, retired Air Force Commander Phil Ehr, flagged the issue. The Broward Supervisor of Elections disputed an initial explanation of clerical error, saying a review found no evidence of any mistake.

Mujica wants Robin Peguero, a former federal prosecutor who raised $800,000 through March 31 and currently faces Eliott Rodriguez in a Democratic Primary for Congressional District 27, to run in Congressional District 28 instead. Ehr filed a complaint with the Florida Elections Commission and his campaign manager Vanessa Brito said they will file a lawsuit Friday, the last day of qualifying, if Mujica remains in the race. Federal officials from Florida must only live in the state, not the district they represent, to qualify for office.

cards.headline: Annette Taddeo enters race for Florida Chief Financial Officer, challenges Blaise Ingoglia
cards.teaser: Democratic former state Sen. Annette Taddeo officially entered the race for Chief Financial Officer on Monday, the opening day of qualifying week.
cards.body:
Democratic former state Sen. Annette Taddeo officially entered the race for Chief Financial Officer during qualifying week, positioning herself as a "watchdog," not a "lapdog," focused on issues such as insurance costs and government accountability. She will challenge appointed Republican CFO Blaise Ingoglia, who is seeking a full term in the Cabinet post.

Qualifying week also produced notable developments in Central Florida. Navy reserve officer and former Trump Pentagon appointee Dan Green launched a campaign in Florida's 9th Congressional District and committed $1 million of his own money to the race. Former state Rep. Daisy Morales filed for the open House District 43 seat, seeking to return to Tallahassee after losing re-election in 2022 and her first comeback bid against now-Rep. Rita Harris two years later. Term-limited state Rep. Susan Valdés filed to run for the Hillsborough County Commission, where she faces incumbent Republican Donna Cameron Cepeda, Hillsborough County School Board Member Stacy Hahn, and Democrat Neil Manimala. All candidate paperwork and filing fees must be submitted to the Division of Elections Office in Tallahassee by noon Friday.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Commissioner Sara Baxter enters Congressional District 22 race
cards.teaser: Republican Sara Baxter is forgoing a re-election bid for the Palm Beach County Commission, where she currently serves as Mayor, to run for Florida's 22nd Congressional District.
cards.body:
Republican Sara Baxter, currently serving as Mayor of the Palm Beach County Commission, has filed paperwork with the Federal Election Commission to run in Florida's 22nd Congressional District. The redrawn district spans parts of Palm Beach and Broward counties and extends across the state into Hendry and Collier counties. Baxter joins eight other GOP candidates in the race: Deborah Adeimy, Casey Askar, David Burck, Michael Carbonara, Terri Hasdorff, Belinda Keiser, Anna Medvedeva and Herbert Wertheim. She won election to the County Commission in 2022, flipping the panel's District 6 seat and currently represents part of western Palm Beach County, including Royal Palm Beach, Wellington, Loxahatchee Groves, the Acreage, Belle Glade and the Glades agricultural region. Prior to winning public office, she worked in healthcare, taught middle school science and worked as a real estate agent.

Baxter raised nearly $146,000 through her County Commission campaign account, the most of any candidate in that contest. President Donald Trump endorsed Baxter for re-election, calling her a "true MAGA Warrior." About 54.6% of voters in the redrawn district supported Trump in 2024. The Palm Beach County Commission on Ethics found probable cause about a year and a half ago that Baxter violated the county ethics code by failing to report gifts, including travel on a private jet partially owned by lobbyist Ron Book to DeSantis' 2023 inauguration and attendance at expensive VIP events. The Commission ultimately dismissed the complaint, concluding the violation appeared inadvertent.

cards.headline: Tampa Mayor Jane Castor pushes for public input on Land Development Code overhaul
cards.teaser: Tampa Mayor Jane Castor encouraged residents to participate in the final public input meeting Monday evening for the Tampa Forward effort to overhaul the city's Land Development Code.
cards.body:
Tampa Forward aims to rewrite the city's Land Development Code, which hasn't had a serious overhaul in decades. The city launched the effort in April 2024 and expects to complete the project in the second half of 2026. The first installment was released for public review earlier this year after discussions with city staff and an advisory team. The current draft proposes changes to simplify existing zoning categories and create new mixed-use districts aimed at walkable development in neighborhoods, corridors and regional centers. It would allow more "missing middle" housing types in some residential and multifamily districts, including duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes, townhomes, cottage homes and courtyard multifamily. The draft would reduce minimum parking requirements and add new development standards for building placement, pedestrian access, street trees, parking location and neighborhood compatibility.

The update comes as Tampa continues to grapple with rapid growth, housing demand, redevelopment pressure and neighborhood concerns. The city is hosting its final public input meeting for the effort Monday evening. Mayor Castor encouraged residents to participate, saying "Your future neighbors definitely have opinions. I've watched this city grow from the inside my entire life. I want to make sure what we're building next is something we're all proud of."

hero.headline: 125 acre brush fire fully contained in western Martin County
hero.teaser: Fire crews have fully contained a 125 acre brush fire that burned in western Martin County.
hero.body:
A 125 acre brush fire that burned in western Martin County has been fully contained, according to Real Radio 92.1. The fire occurred in the western part of the county.

Fire crews worked to bring the blaze under control. The fire has now been fully contained.

cards.headline: Stuart lawmaker expects legal challenges to Florida property tax referendum before November vote
cards.teaser: The referendum on lowering property taxes in Florida may face a state constitutional challenge on several fronts, according to former Florida state Sen.
cards.body:
A Florida property tax referendum faces potential constitutional challenges on multiple fronts, according to former state Sen. Jeff Brandes. The referendum would raise the homestead exemption for homeowners to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, with voters set to decide the measure on Election Day in November. Brandes told WPTV on Monday that he sees questions about home rule, unfunded mandates and taxing uniformity. In a Saturday social media post, he identified five possible legal challenges: ballot language, equal protection, uniformity, home rule and unfunded mandates.

State Rep. Toby Overdorf, R-Stuart, told WPTV after the vote was approved in special session last week that he expects a legal challenge because this is not a normal bill but a joint resolution that changes the Constitution. Multiple challenges could put the courts under pressure with the November vote scheduled. Brandes said the courts will have to consolidate these cases to address a handful of really interesting questions. At this point, no lawsuits have been filed against the referendum, but many expect that to happen once the actual question for voters is completed.

cards.headline: 36,000 square foot mural now faces Florida Turnpike drivers in Martin County
cards.teaser: A massive 36,000 square foot mural is now visible to drivers on the Florida Turnpike in Martin County.
cards.body:
Drivers on the Florida Turnpike in Martin County can now see a 36,000 square foot mural facing the highway. The large scale artwork is positioned to be visible from the turnpike.

The mural spans 36,000 square feet, making it a significant visual landmark for motorists traveling through Martin County on the turnpike.

cards.headline: FPL brings 2026 infrastructure upgrades to Martin County and Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: Florida Power & Light is implementing infrastructure upgrades across Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin Counties in 2026.
cards.body:
Florida Power & Light has brought 2026 infrastructure upgrades to Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin Counties. The utility company is implementing improvements to its electrical infrastructure across the three Treasure Coast counties.

The upgrades are part of FPL's 2026 infrastructure improvement plan for the region. The work covers all three counties in the Treasure Coast area.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County implements 45-day anchoring limits to combat abandoned vessels
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County has new restrictions limiting how long boaters can anchor in Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor near the South Causeway Bridge.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County implemented two anchor limitation areas in the Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor near the South Causeway Bridge on June 1. Under the new restrictions, a person may not anchor a vessel for more than 45 consecutive days in any six-month period in any anchoring limitation area without leaving all anchoring limitation areas for at least 24 hours.

Erick Gill with St. Lucie County said the Fish and Wildlife Commission collected around two dozen derelict vessels last year. Gill said the restrictions will help make the waterways more navigable and keep the vessel highway clear and free for other vessels to come and go. He noted there are over 4,000 species of animals, plants, and birds that live in the lagoon. The restrictions will help protect the lagoon by avoiding pollutants from diesel and oil tanks and holding tanks from getting into the water.

cards.headline: 2-year-old drowns in Fort Pierce after being found unresponsive in pool
cards.teaser: A 2-year-old drowned over the weekend in Fort Pierce after the child was found unresponsive in a swimming pool at a home on Citrus Avenue.
cards.body:
A 2-year-old drowned over the weekend in Fort Pierce after being found unresponsive in a swimming pool, police said. The drowning occurred at a home in the 2600 block of Citrus Avenue on Saturday. According to a preliminary investigation, while family members were inside the residence, the child was able to unlock a door and leave the home unnoticed. When family members realized the child was missing, they began searching the property and discovered the child unresponsive in a swimming pool.

Family members immediately began administering first aid until the arrival of Fort Pierce police officers, who worked to save the child. The child was taken to a local hospital for emergency medical treatment but later succumbed to his injuries. The incident remains under investigation. This latest drowning comes after a 2-year-old drowned in a Greenacres canal in March and another 2-year-old drowned in Palm Beach Gardens in May.

cards.headline: 6.4 magnitude earthquake off Cuba reportedly felt in Florida
cards.teaser: A strong earthquake off the northwest coast of Cuba on Monday was reportedly felt in Florida.
cards.body:
A 6.4 magnitude earthquake occurred about 73 miles west-northwest of Mantua on the northwest side of Cuba on Monday, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. The strong earthquake was reportedly felt in Florida.

The quake happened off the Cuban coast and was strong enough that residents in Florida reported feeling it. The earthquake measured 6.4 on the magnitude scale.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County implements 45-day anchoring limits in Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor
hero.body:
St. Lucie County rolled out new anchoring restrictions on June 1 to address growing concerns about abandoned vessels in local waterways. The county designated two anchor limitation areas in the Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor near the South Causeway Bridge. Under these new rules, boaters cannot anchor a vessel for more than 45 consecutive days within any six-month period without leaving all anchor limitation areas for at least 24 hours.

County officials say the restrictions are necessary because of an increase in derelict vessels cluttering the waterways. Last year alone, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission collected approximately two dozen abandoned vessels from these areas. According to Erick Gill with St. Lucie County, the new regulations will improve navigation for boaters. "We need to make sure that highway for vessels is clear and free for other vessels to come and go," Gill said. Maintaining clear waterways allows commercial and recreational boaters to move safely through these important channels.

Abandoned vessels pose serious environmental risks to the lagoon ecosystem. When derelict boats remain in the water for extended periods, they can leak harmful substances into the water. James Beams with St. Lucie County Port, Inlet and Beaches explained the concern: "There's a lot of environmental concern with the diesel and oil tanks and then holding tanks." These leaks threaten the delicate balance of the lagoon's natural environment. By limiting how long vessels can remain anchored in one location, the county hopes to prevent pollutants from contaminating the water and damaging the surrounding ecosystem.

The Indian River Lagoon supports remarkable biodiversity, hosting over 4,000 species of animals, plants, and birds. Gill emphasized the importance of protecting this unique environment, stating "We want to make sure we're protecting it." The new anchoring restrictions represent a dual approach to waterway management by addressing both navigation concerns and environmental protection. Boaters interested in the specific locations of the anchor limitation areas can obtain a site map from St. Lucie County. These new rules aim to preserve the environmental health of the Indian River Lagoon while keeping the waterways accessible and safe for all users.

cards.headline: 2-year-old drowns in Fort Pierce pool after leaving home unnoticed
cards.teaser: A 2-year-old child drowned over the weekend after unlocking a door and leaving a home unnoticed, then being found unresponsive in a swimming pool.
cards.body:
A 2-year-old drowned in Fort Pierce on Saturday after being found unresponsive in a swimming pool at a home in the 2600 block of Citrus Avenue, police said. According to a preliminary investigation, while family members were inside the residence, the child unlocked a door and left the home unnoticed. When family members realized the child was missing, they searched the property and discovered the child unresponsive in the swimming pool. Family members immediately began administering first aid until Fort Pierce police officers arrived and worked to save the child.

The child was taken to a local hospital for emergency medical treatment but later succumbed to injuries. Police said the incident remains under investigation. This drowning follows a 2-year-old who drowned in a Greenacres canal in March and another 2-year-old who drowned in Palm Beach Gardens in May.

Florida Power & Light is bringing infrastructure upgrades to St. Lucie County in 2026. The utility company is also conducting improvements in Indian River and Martin Counties.

cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce pastor faces child neglect charges after children were found living in unsafe conditions.

A Fort Pierce pastor has been charged with child neglect after children were found living in unsafe conditions. The charges follow an investigation into the living environment where the children resided.

Details about the specific conditions and the number of children affected were reported by authorities investigating the case.

cards.headline: Suspect arrested in burglary spree at Spanish Lakes in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County deputies arrested a suspect connected to a series of burglaries in the Spanish Lakes community.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County deputies arrested a suspect tied to a burglary spree in Spanish Lakes, according to the Sheriff's Office. The arrest follows multiple break-ins at the 55-plus community.

The suspect was connected to a string of burglaries that targeted homes in the Spanish Lakes area. The Sheriff's Office said no one was home during the break-ins.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested for swinging bat at children on bicycles
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie man was arrested and accused of swinging a bat at children who were riding bicycles.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man was arrested after allegedly swinging a bat at children riding bicycles. The incident led to criminal charges against the man.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce will not renew City Attorney Sara Hedges contract
cards.teaser: The City of Fort Pierce has decided not to renew the contract of City Attorney Sara Hedges.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce will not renew the contract of City Attorney Sara Hedges. The decision was made by the city regarding Hedges' position.

The city attorney's contract is set to expire, and Fort Pierce officials have chosen not to extend it. The decision affects the legal representation for the city government.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County implements 45-day anchoring limits to combat abandoned vessels
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County has new restrictions for boaters anchoring in the Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor, limiting stays to 45 consecutive days in any six-month period.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County established new anchoring restrictions effective June 1 to address the growing problem of abandoned vessels in local waterways. The county designated two anchor limitation areas in the Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor near the South Causeway Bridge. Under these new rules, boaters cannot anchor a vessel for more than 45 consecutive days within any six-month period without departing all anchoring limitation areas for at least 24 hours.

The abandoned vessel problem has become increasingly visible in St. Lucie County's waterways. According to Erick Gill with St. Lucie County, the Florida Wildlife Commission collected approximately two dozen derelict vessels during the previous year. The new anchoring restrictions aim to keep the waterways clear and navigable for legitimate vessel traffic. "We need to make sure that highway for vessels is clear and free for other vessels to come and go," Gill said. By limiting how long vessels can remain anchored, the county hopes to prevent boats from being left in place indefinitely.

Environmental protection serves as another key motivation for the restrictions. James Beams with St. Lucie County Port, Inlet and Beaches explained that abandoned vessels pose significant environmental risks when left unattended for extended periods. Boats sitting in the water can leak diesel fuel, oil, and other contents from holding tanks, threatening water quality in the lagoon. These pollutants can harm the diverse ecosystem that depends on clean water. Gill emphasized that preventing these contaminants from entering the water is essential for protecting the lagoon's inhabitants. The area is home to over 4,000 species of animals, plants, and birds that rely on this aquatic environment.

To help boaters understand where these restrictions apply, St. Lucie County has published a detailed site map showing the anchor limitation areas. Boaters operating in the Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor should review this map to ensure compliance with the new regulations. The restrictions represent the county's effort to balance the needs of boaters who use the waterways with the imperative to protect the environment and maintain navigable channels for all water traffic.

cards.headline: Florida Power & Light bringing infrastructure upgrades to Indian River County in 2026
cards.teaser: Florida Power & Light is bringing infrastructure upgrades to Indian River County in 2026.
cards.body:
Florida Power & Light is bringing infrastructure upgrades to Indian River County in 2026. The utility company announced the upgrades on Monday, which will also extend to St. Lucie and Martin Counties.

The infrastructure improvements are part of FPL's 2026 upgrade program for the Treasure Coast region. The announcement was made on Monday, June 8.

The upgrades are designed to improve electrical service reliability for residents and businesses across the three-county area. Indian River County, which includes Vero Beach, Sebastian, and Fellsmere, will benefit from the planned improvements.

FPL has not yet released specific details about which neighborhoods or areas within Indian River County will receive the upgrades first or the exact timeline for completion of the work.

cards.headline: 2-year-old child drowns in Fort Pierce swimming pool
cards.teaser: A 2-year-old drowned over the weekend in Fort Pierce after being found unresponsive in a swimming pool at a home on Citrus Avenue.
cards.body:
A 2-year-old drowned over the weekend in Fort Pierce after being found unresponsive in a swimming pool at a home in the 2600 block of Citrus Avenue on Saturday. According to police, a preliminary investigation revealed that while family members were inside the residence, the child was able to unlock a door and leave the home unnoticed. When family members realized the child was missing, they began searching the property and discovered the child unresponsive in the swimming pool.

Family members immediately began administering first aid until Fort Pierce police officers arrived and worked to save the child. The child was taken to a local hospital for emergency medical treatment but later succumbed to his injuries. The incident remains under investigation. This latest drowning comes after a 2-year-old drowned in a Greenacres canal in March and another 2-year-old drowned in Palm Beach Gardens in May.

cards.headline: Florida property tax referendum could face up to 5 constitutional challenges
cards.teaser: The referendum on lowering property taxes in Florida may face multiple state constitutional challenges, according to former state Senator Jeff Brandes.
cards.body:
Former Florida state Sen. Jeff Brandes identified five potential constitutional challenges to the property tax referendum during an Monday interview. The possible legal challenges include ballot language, equal protection, uniformity, home rule, and unfunded mandates. In a Saturday social media post, Brandes outlined his concerns about the referendum, which would raise the homestead exemption for homeowners to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Brandes noted questions about home rule, unfunded mandates, and taxing uniformity among the constitutional issues the referendum could face.

State Rep. Toby Overdorf, R-Stuart, emphasized that the referendum differs from typical legislation because it is a joint resolution that changes the Constitution. After the vote was approved in special session last week, Overdorf said he expects a legal challenge. However, he cautioned that multiple challenges could pressure the courts ahead of the Election Day vote scheduled for November. Brandes said the courts will need to consolidate the cases. As of now, no lawsuits have been filed against the referendum, though many expect legal challenges once voters see the final ballot language.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Commissioner Sara Baxter announces run for Congress
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County Mayor and District 6 Commissioner Sara Baxter announced Monday she will run for Congress in Florida's newly drawn District 22.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County Commissioner Sara Baxter announced Monday that she will run for Congress in Florida's newly drawn District 22, confirming she will drop out of the county commission race to pursue the seat. Baxter said: "Washington needs more fighters who are focused on delivering for their district. The creation of the new congressional district blesses me with the opportunity to work with President Trump to stop illegal migrant crime, protect our elections, cut taxes, slash red tape and bloated bureaucracy, protect hard working farmers, our food supply chain, support our great military and veterans, and defend our Second Amendment rights."

Baxter was elected to the District 6 seat in 2022 representing parts of western Palm Beach County including Royal Palm Beach, Loxahatchee Groves, Acreage, Wellington, Westlake, Belle Glade, South Bay, Pahokee, and West Lake Worth. A self-proclaimed political outsider, she held no political office before her election and previously ran a small business with her husband, Brian. President Donald Trump has endorsed Baxter in her reelection campaign. Her announcement creates an open race for the District 6 county commission seat. Congressional District 22 is expected to be one of South Florida's closely watched races in the 2026 election cycle.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach man to cheer Cape Verde at World Cup in Miami
cards.teaser: Eridjon Dacruz of West Palm Beach is headed to Miami this month to cheer on Cape Verde, one of the smallest countries ever to qualify for the World Cup.
cards.body:
Eridjon Dacruz, a West Palm Beach resident who grew up in Cape Verde, will attend his country's World Cup game against Uruguay in Miami this month. Cape Verde, an archipelago of 10 islands off the African coast, gained independence from Portugal in the 1970s and has a population of half a million people. The nation's soccer team, known as the Tubarão Azul or Blue Sharks, qualified for the World Cup for the first time ever, making Cape Verdeans ecstatic about their achievement. Dacruz received his ticket as an anniversary gift from his girlfriend, who presented him with a handwritten note during their anniversary dinner saying "I'm going to the World Cup."

Cape Verde opens the tournament against Spain, one of the tournament favorites, before facing Uruguay. Dacruz expressed confidence in his team's ability to advance, saying "All we have to do is win a couple of games and we'll get far." The World Cup qualification will provide Cape Verde's soccer federation with more than $10 million to help develop the next generation of players. During hurricane season, the islands are frequently referenced in weather coverage, as tropical systems often form near Cape Verde before tracking west across the Atlantic toward the U.S.

cards.headline: 42-year-old arrested in fatal shooting of Plantation father in Boca Raton
cards.teaser: Willie Byrd Jr., 42, of Boynton Beach was arrested Friday in the fatal shooting of Arman Motiwalla, 37, who was gunned down in a Boca Raton parking lot in April.
cards.body:
A 42-year-old Boynton Beach man has been arrested in connection with the fatal shooting of 37-year-old Arman Motiwalla, a Plantation father who was found dead in a Boca Raton parking lot in April. Willie Byrd Jr. was charged with first-degree murder with a firearm and is being held at Palm Beach County Jail. Motiwalla was discovered with multiple gunshot wounds next to his car around 1:45 a.m. on April 8 in the parking lot of 350 Camino Gardens Boulevard. According to a probable cause affidavit from the Boca Raton Police Department, surveillance footage captured the shooting on the evening of April 7, and Motiwalla's Apple Watch recorded his last heartbeat at 8:25 p.m.

The investigation revealed Byrd drove a silver Chrysler 200 with stolen license plates to conceal the vehicle's identity. Surveillance data and license-plate readers tracked Byrd from his Boynton Beach residence to the Boca Raton crime scene and back home. A search warrant on Byrd's vehicle uncovered a Post-It note containing the Camino Gardens address, Motiwalla's name, personal address and his fiance's name, along with 9mm magazines, ammunition, Western Union receipts and Chase Bank account information. Cell phone data analysis revealed Byrd had surveilled Motiwalla's workplace. Motiwalla had filed a whistleblower complaint against his former employer, Innovative Partners L.P., in 2025.
